findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: The facility has milk open with no date marking. The facility manager knew the open date and placed it on the container. The violation is considered corrected on site.  Practice good date marking habits for all TCS (temperature control for safety) foods. 

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed interior baffles of the ice machine to have a heavy accumulation of mold. Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 11/1/21.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

PIC does not have CFM license; however, does have a food handlers license. Provided additional paperwork regarding CFM classes through SCDPH in the 2020 year. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection in 2018.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11  (Pf) Working container of toxic substance not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

Observed unknown toxic substance to not have proper label underneath a cabinent in main cafe area. Discussed proper labeling of all toxic substance spray bottles with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12  (C) Food storage containers are not labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

Observed bulk item to be in a container without a label. Discussed applying common name of items on bulk containers of food items with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection in 2018.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed multiple single-service articles to not be protected from contamination. Items were not in original packaging and/or not placed upside down in order to protect against cross-contamination. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (Pf) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability

Observed no working buckets of chlorine bleach sanitizer throughout facility. Discussed need to have at least one working sanitization bucket during hours of operation. COS.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

Observed areas of reach-in freezer and reach-in cooler to have employee items mixed with customer items for facility. Discussed with PIC: Designating an area of each equipment to store employee belongings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: No full time food manager for the establishment. Follow up in 90 days.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed a bulk powder container with no label. The container was labeled with the proper name during the inspection.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Observed no chlorine test kit for the facility. Provide a chlorine test kit.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the panini press soiled. 2) Observed the microwave soiled. Clean the food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service knives intermixed in a cup. Make sure to have the handle extended out of the food. 
This violation was corrected during the routine inspection.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no full time food manager. Provide a full time manager.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Observed no bleach test kit for the facility. Obtain a bleach test kit.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed a knife stored underneath the panini press. This is not a proper practice. Store clean utensils in a clean and sanitized area.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text:
750.100 - Deli turkey labeled 10/17 in the top holding area of the prep cooler was slimy and discolored. Manager stated the product was not in the cooler longer than 3 or 4 days. The product was not in sound condition and was not properly labeled. Turkey was discarded during the inspection.

Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - A) An open package of ham in the 2 door cooler as observed without a date mark. Manager was unsure as to when the package was opened. Ham was discarded in the trash.
B) Ziploc bag of pre-cooked sausage had a date mark of 10/8 on it. Sausages were discarded during the inspection.
C) Frozen, heat and serve soup was placed in the cooler on Sunday to thaw for use this week. Soup was labeled during the inspection. 
D) Open gallons of milk in the coffee cooler were not dated. Manager stated products were opened on Saturday. Milks were labeled during the inspection.
E) Container of questionable deli turkey in the top holding area of the prep cooler was observed with a date mark of 10/17. Manager stated all other products in the top holding area of the prep cooler were fresh today, but the turkey was inaccurately labeled. Turkey was discarded (see #1a).

Refrigerated potentially hazardous, ready to eat food shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
Make sure foods are labeled properly and not relabeled for any reason to ensure foods are used or discarded within 7 days.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750.280 - Stir spoons sitting on top of vanilla powder mix were soiled with buildup. Cleaning/sanitizing and storage of spoons were discussed with cafe manager.

Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop was observed sitting on top of the ice bin at the front counter. Top of the bin was observed with dust accumulation. Proper storage of the scoop in a clean container was discussed.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) single basin sink at front counter (buildup);
B) base of blender and surface of pitcher where it attaches to the base (splash and mold);   and
C) under toaster oven (dust).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Clean under equipment on counters daily.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Far left faucet in women's restroom did not have hot water. All other sinks in the women's room and men's room had both hot and cold water. Repair the sink in the women's room.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - A) Paper towels were not present at the back handsink. 

Maintain a supply of soap and paper towels at both handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

B) Front handsink was soiled with buildup.

Clean the handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - A) Floor drain and cover under the single basin sink up front was soiled with buildup. Clean the drain and cover daily/as needed.

B) Debris was observed under the 2 door cooler in back. Clean under coolers and other equipment daily/as needed.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Damp mops were observed stored in the third compartment of the 3 part sink. Manager was advised to cease storage in the sink. Mops may be stored on edges of the mop bucket as long as they have the ability to be spread out and dry properly. Otherwise, mops needs to be hung or inverted in the utility room at the mopsink. 
Mops were positioned (fanned out) on the mop bucket to allow for proper drying during the inspection.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment must be stored properly and in a manner that will not potentially contaminate food.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - Tupperware of vanilla powder mix was unlabeled. Provide a label for all powders and liquids not stored in original product containers/packaging.

Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the original container or package, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Wiping cloth was observed on the counter by coffee machine. Wiping cloth was placed in sanitizer solution.

Store wet wiping cloths in solutions between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Change sanitizer solutions in buckets every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Use test strips to verify sanitizer concentration is 200-400ppm quat.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Employee coat was hanging on the storage shelves next to single service items and food. Coat was moved to a chair in the seating area.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings separate from food prep/food storage areas and any food related items (i.e. clean equipment, single service items) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.
